;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**[[Kouré shooting]]
***The [[Boko Haram|Islamic State's West Africa Province]] claims responsibility for last month's attack in [[Kouré]], [[Niger]], which resulted in the death of six [[France|French]] aid workers and two Nigerian citizens. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-niger-security/islamic-state-claims-killing-of-french-aid-workers-in-niger-idUSKBN2682JX (Reuters)]
*[[Iraqi insurgency (2017–present)|Iraqi insurgency]]
**[[2020 Iraq attacks]]
***A bomb hits a convoy, killing four members of the [[Popular Mobilization Forces]] in [[Kirkuk Governorate|Kirkuk]]. [http://ninanews.com/Website/News/Details?key=856988 (National Iraqi News Agency)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[September 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***The [[Taliban]] kills 32 members of the security forces and two civilians, and injures another 17 security forces, in four attacks across [[Afghanistan]]. At least 84 Taliban militants also died in the attacks. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan-166385 (TOLOnews)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
***The [[Economy of New Zealand|economy]] enters [[recession]] for the first time since 1987 after the country's [[GDP]] declined by 12.2% between April and June, amid a nationwide lockdown and travel bans due to COVID-19. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-54186359 (BBC News)]
**[[Shortages related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***An additional 150 million children live in [[Multidimensional Poverty Index|multidimensional]] [[poverty]] since the start of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] earlier this year. The analysis by [[UNICEF]] and [[Save the Children]] is based on shortcomings in education, health, housing, nutrition, sanitation, and water. [https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/international/2020/09/17/fgn17-un-children-poverty.html (PTI via ''The Week'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Teddy]] strengthens into a [[Category 3 hurricane]] over the [[Atlantic Ocean]] and heads to [[Bermuda]], which is recovering from [[Hurricane Paulette]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/hurricane-teddy-strengthens-to-a-category-2-storm-over-the-open-atlantic/2020/09/17/9ab0ffe2-f8c4-11ea-85f7-5941188a98cd_story.html (''The Washington Post'')] [https://weather.com/storms/hurricane/news/2020-09-16-hurricane-teddy-forecast-bermuda-atlantic-canada (The Weather Channel)]
*[[2020 California wildfires]]
**A firefighter dies in the [[El Dorado Fire]] while battling blazes in the [[San Bernardino National Forest]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/sep/18/california-fires-oregon-deaths-rain-humid-weather (''The Guardian'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]]
*****[[Secretary of State for Health and Social Care|Health Secretary]] [[Matt Hancock]] announces that temporary restrictions will be in place in [[Newcastle upon Tyne|Newcastle]], [[Gateshead]], [[Sunderland]], [[Northumberland]], [[South Tyneside]], [[North Tyneside]], and the [[Durham County Council]] area effective at midnight tonight due to "concerning rates of infection." Almost two million people in North-east England will be banned from meeting with other households. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-tyne-54188766 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a record increase of 770 new cases and ten deaths since the end of national [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] in May, thus bringing the cumulative totals to 66,396 confirmed cases and 1,888 deaths. Today also marks the official start of the 2020/2021 public school year, which began with in-person classes nationwide. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/199_DGS_boletim_20200917.pdf (DGS)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
****A two-month-old baby dies of COVID-19 in [[Michigan]], the youngest known fatality in the state thus far. [https://www.mlive.com/public-interest/2020/09/2-month-old-dies-of-coronavirus-in-michigan.html (MLive.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Texas]]
****[[List of governors of Texas|Texas Governor]] [[Greg Abbott]] eases restrictions on retail stores, gyms, and restaurants. Bars, however, remain closed. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/09/17/texas-pushes-forward-with-business-reopenings-as-coronavirus-cases-hospitalizations-slide-gov-abbott-says.html (CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
***[[India]] reports another record jump in daily infections, with 97,894 cases reported in the last 24 hours, as shown by data from the health ministry. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/covid-19-india-record-daily-new-cases-coronavirus-13119906 (CNA)]

;International relations
*International response to the [[2020 Belarusian protests]], [[Belarus–European Union relations]]
**[[government of Poland|Polish]] [[Prime Minister of Poland|Prime Minister]] [[Mateusz Morawiecki]] proposes a [[Euro|€]]1 billion ([[United States dollar|US$]]1.2 billion) [[stabilization fund]] by the [[European Central Bank]] to revitalize the [[Economy of Belarus|Belarusian economy]] amid the protests. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200917-poland-proposes-billion-euro-eu-fund-for-belarus (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Territorial disputes in the South China Sea]]
**[[France]], [[Germany]], and the [[United Kingdom]] issue a joint ''note verbale'' to the [[United Nations]] rejecting [[China]]'s claims to the [[South China Sea]], and supporting the ruling in ''[[Philippines v. China]]'' that said the historic rights per the [[nine-dash line]] ran counter to the [[United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea]]. However the statement says that on "territorial sovereignty" they "take no position". [https://www.cnnphilippines.com/news/2020/9/18/France-Germany-United-Kingdom-reject-China-South-China-Sea.html (CNN Philippines)]

;Law and crime
*[[Women in Afghanistan]]
**[[President of Afghanistan|President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]] signs an amendment allowing mother's names to appear on their child's [[birth certificate]], after discussion on the law was delayed by the [[National Assembly (Afghanistan)|National Assembly]] last week. The move is seen as a "significant milestone" for women's rights, following Afghan tradition stating that using a woman's name in public brings shame on their family. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-09-18/afghan-government-passes-law-mother-name-birth-certificate/12634162 (ABC Australia)]
*A court in [[Hong Kong]] convicts an 81-year-old man for stabbing [[Pro-democracy camp (Hong Kong)|pro-democracy]] activist [[Leung Kwok-hung]], also known as "Long Hair". Magistrate Cheang Kei-hong adjourned sentencing to October 13 and praised the perpetrator for "loving society", while also commenting that Leung was not hurt seriously. [https://www.thestandard.com.hk/section-news/section/4/223079/Old-man-gets-court-praise-for-attack-on-'Long-Hair' (''The Standard'')]
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]]
**[[United States Attorney General|U.S. Attorney General]] [[William Barr]] tells prosecutors to aggressively charge people arrested at recent demonstrations across the country, even suggesting including a [[sedition]] charge, which is usually reserved for those who have plotted a threat that posed imminent danger to the government. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2020/sep/16/bill-barr-sedition-charges-protests (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Bolivian general election]]
**[[President of Bolivia|Interim president]] [[Jeanine Áñez]] withdraws from the presidential race, saying the opposition needs to consolidate to beat frontrunner [[Luis Arce]], who is representing deposed President [[Evo Morales]]' party [[Movement for Socialism (Bolivia)|Movement for Socialism]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bolivia-election-anez/bolivian-interim-president-anez-withdraws-from-election-race-with-socialists-ahead-in-polls-idUSKBN26900V?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Sports
*[[Armand Duplantis]] sets the outdoor [[pole vault]] world record at 6.15 metres at the [[Stadio Olimpico]] in [[Rome]], eclipsing the previous record held for 26 years by [[Sergey Bubka]]. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-09-18/armand-duplantis-breaks-sergey-bubkas-pole-vault-world-record/12677616 (ABC)]
